gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Windows switches a Bluetooth speaker that supports the Hands-Free Profile to mono playback at 8 kHz or 16 kHz as soon as any app opens that speaker's microphone input. Microsoft says this happens on Windows 11 and that Windows 10 discards the stereo stream outright. Microsoft also lists only SBC, AAC, aptX Classic and aptX Adaptive (aptX Adaptive only on select Qualcomm radios) as Windows A2DP codecs, so a mic-less, A2DP-only speaker such as the Creative Pebble Pro, or a wired USB-C connection, avoids the problem.
standout_why: I read stackandvalue.com (cited) in full. It lists only connection types (Pebble Pro 'connects over USB-C, Bluetooth 5.3, or a 3.5mm cable', Z407, R1280DBs, Klipsch) and says nothing about Bluetooth profiles, Hands-Free/HFP, codecs or what Windows does when a mic is opened. I could not check the other cited pages. TechRadar, Tom's Hardware, Tom's Guide (the roundup and the Pebble Pro review) and PC Gamer each returned only a title of about 110 to 130 characters to the fetcher, and Wired blocked the fetch, so those pages may cover it. ChatGPT's own answers only say Bluetooth 'can introduce audio delay' and suggest wired for gaming and calls. They never name the HFP mono switch, and the second chat even offers 'Work and video calls' as a use case. I scored 2 rather than 3 because most of the rival pages could not be checked.
decides: For a PC used for both media and calls, pick a speaker that is A2DP-only with no built-in mic, or one with a wired USB-C audio input. That confirms the Creative Pebble Pro (A2DP only, SBC, USB audio, no built-in mic) as the safe default. A single portable speaker with a hands-free mic, such as the Marshall Emberton III, is a poor PC choice when calls matter. The moment Teams or Discord opens its mic, Windows drops the speaker to mono 8 kHz or 16 kHz, and the Emberton III has no wired audio input to fall back on (its USB-C is listed only for charging). The Creative T60 lists HFP alongside A2DP, so Windows 11 creates a mic input for it. Over Bluetooth, keep the PC's default mic set to something else, or use the T60's USB-C audio. A further point for the Pebble Pro: the 30 W RMS figure needs a separate 30 W USB PD adapter, which is not included. Powered from a PC port it is 10 W RMS.

findings.label: Windows A2DP codecs, in the order Windows picks them
findings.value: aptX Adaptive (lossless): Windows 11 24H2 only, 'only supported on select Windows devices with compatible Qualcomm Bluetooth radios'; AAC: Windows 11 21H2 and later, not supported on Windows 10; aptX Classic: Windows 10 1507 and later; SBC: Windows 10 1507 and later. LDAC is not in the table.
findings.source_title: Bluetooth Classic Audio - Windows drivers | Microsoft Learn
findings.note: Microsoft: 'Windows starts from the top of the list, and chooses the first codec supported by both the host and the audio device for A2DP playback.' Page ms.date 2024-11-14, updated 2025-07-18.

findings.label: Hands-Free Profile audio format on Windows
findings.value: Mono only: narrowband 8 kHz (SBC) or wideband 16 kHz (mSBC)
findings.source_title: Bluetooth Classic Audio - Windows drivers | Microsoft Learn
findings.note: Microsoft: 'HFP supports concurrent monaural capture (microphone) and monaural playback'. Also: 'Some wideband capable audio devices aren't compatible with the Bluetooth radio in select Windows devices, causing these devices to revert to narrowband mode.'

findings.label: When Windows 11 switches from stereo A2DP to mono HFP
findings.value: When any app opens the device's microphone input, or creates a playback stream in the Communications category
findings.source_title: Bluetooth Classic Audio - Windows drivers | Microsoft Learn
findings.note: Microsoft: 'If an audio device supports HFP, a single output and single input endpoint are created'. 'if media is playing and the device is in A2DP mode, and then the microphone is opened, the device switches to HFP mode.' Other audio is 'resampled to match the HFP endpoint'.

findings.label: Windows 10 behaviour in HFP mode
findings.value: Stereo output is discarded while the device is in Hands-Free mode
findings.source_title: Bluetooth Classic Audio - Windows drivers | Microsoft Learn
findings.note: Microsoft: 'any audio streaming to the stereo output is discarded.' On Windows 10, separate '{Device Name} Stereo' and '{Device Name} Hands-Free' endpoints are created.

findings.label: Bluetooth LE Audio on Windows
findings.value: Introduced in Windows 11 22H2 (KB5026446). The LC3 codec must come from the hardware vendor's audio driver stack or Bluetooth controller. Stereo music and game playback formats go up to 48 kHz, 2 channels, 96 kbps.
findings.source_title: Bluetooth Low Energy (LE) Audio - Windows drivers | Microsoft Learn
findings.note: This means LE Audio-ready speakers only get LE Audio on PCs whose Bluetooth hardware and drivers implement it. It is not a fix for every PC.

findings.label: Bluetooth profile, codec and mic
findings.value: Bluetooth 5.3; codec SBC only; profile '(A2DP) Wireless Stereo Bluetooth' only; no built-in mic listed (has a 3-pole microphone port and a 4-pole headset port); 'USB audio and power'
findings.source_title: Creative Pebble Pro Minimalist 2.0 USB-C Computer Speakers with Bluetooth 5.3 and Customizable RGB Lighting - Creative Labs (United States)
findings.note: No HFP is listed, so by Microsoft's rules no Bluetooth mic input is created and playback stays on A2DP.

findings.label: Power output by power source

findings.source_title: Creative Pebble Pro - Creative Labs (United States)
findings.note: As quoted on Creative's spec section.
